one_line_contribution: A contamination experiment that manipulates writer identity rather than content: relabelled-failure items are planted in one fixed bank at a fixed rate by five writers placed on a measured policy-agreement axis, and the claim is that harm to a reader rises with writer-reader proximity (peaking on the reader's own failures, reversing when the reader is swapped) while read-time detectability falls on the same diagonal, so that a foreign-backbone judge filters harm the reader's own judgment cannot.
closest_prior_work: Two verified papers split the claim between them. (a) arXiv:2606.24428 (verified by id; 'Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap: An Execute-Distill-Verify Paradigm for Agentic Experience Learning', 2026-06-23) already names self-confirmatory error in agentic experience construction as the problem and already prescribes the proposal's remedy - multiple heterogeneous agents verifying experience before it is stored - with reported gains over strong baselines. It does not, from its abstract, measure a proximity gradient, run a mirror reader, or score a judge x writer detection table, so it does not scoop P1/P2/P3; but it does mean the practical payload of P5 ('use a foreign model to filter the bank') is an existing recipe, not a discovery, which caps the significance of the proposal's most useful arm. (b) arXiv:2502.04313 (verified by id; 'Great Models Think Alike and this Undermines AI Oversight') makes the general form of the detection claim - similar models make correlated mistakes, so using another model for oversight is risky in proportion to similarity - which is exactly P3's mechanism one level up, with a similarity metric already in hand; the proposal's contribution against it is the agent-experience stimulus and the harm-side consequence, not the mechanism. Add the documented self-detection literature the proposal never cites: arXiv:2507.02778 (Self-Correction Bench: models fix identical errors attributed to an external source but not in their own output) and arXiv:2410.21819 (self-preference bias in LLM-as-a-judge tracks familiarity/perplexity, not quality). Against that background, P3 is a transposition of a known effect to a new stimulus. The verified arXiv:2607.10608 (Compliance Trap) is a weaker threat than the proposal fears: it varies the reader and not the writer and has no read-time detector, so the harm half (P1, P2) does remain unmeasured in the agent-memory literature I could verify.
strongest_objection: The proximity manipulation does not isolate proximity from item text, so the headline can be confirmed and still not mean what the title says. pi(Q-self) is 1.0 by construction (the writer is the reader's own collection policy, probed on the reader's own k=0 states), so the axis has its anchor at a definitional ceiling, and Q-self items are simultaneously the highest-likelihood, most stylistically self-similar text in the whole experiment. A simple imitation account - a reader copies the items its own decoder assigns high likelihood to, regardless of who wrote them - predicts the entire harm ordering, the mirror reversal, and the diagonal detection deficit, and the design never measures the mediator (per-item reader log-likelihood/perplexity, matched across writers). The two arms meant to break this tie make it worse: Q-prox-S disables thinking and swaps the ReAct template, which is a format change the proposal itself declares out of scope as a separate axis (thoughts_do_not_travel), and Q-prox-T raises temperature until pi drops 0.15, which degrades text coherence as well as agreement. So P2's 'proximity, not backbone' contrast is confounded with format and with item quality, and P1's proximity reading is confounded with self-likelihood. Second-order but real: P3 is near-entailed as the entailment check says - the 5 percent false-rejection point is calibrated only on Q's clean expert items, so ordinary self-text leniency (arXiv:2410.21819) produces a diagonal deficit arithmetically, and the judge-overall-recall covariate removes a main effect, not that leniency. Third: every margin rests on an extrapolated half-width (8 x sqrt(1/s1+1/s2)) applied to a +/-8 floor measured at 2 seeds; the game-level variance component does not shrink with seeds and the arms differ in bank content, so the claimed +/-3.3 at 12v12 is asserted rather than derived from a variance decomposition of Measurements A and C.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Measure and report the mediator: per-contaminant log-likelihood under reader Q, and add one writer cell that is far in backbone but matched to Q-self in reader-likelihood (or reweight the E-self pool to match the Q-self likelihood distribution). If harm tracks likelihood rather than pi, that is the real finding and the design should be able to say so. (2) Replace Q-prox-S: hold format fixed (thinking on, same template) and get the pi drop from a different sampling policy or a checkpoint/prompt perturbation, so P2 is not a format contrast; report item-text statistics (length, thought-token share, invalid-command rate) per writer, since 'stylistic distance is equal across writers' is currently asserted, not measured. (3) Calibrate each judge's operating point per writer column on that writer's own clean successes (collect clean items for E and G, not only Q), or subtract the clean-item self-preference gap from each deficit, so P3 measures failure detection rather than familiarity. (4) Add the authorship-attribution control the self-correction literature demands: the same masked items shown to judge Q labelled as its own versus as another agent's - this separates text familiarity from attribution at near-zero cost and is what makes the result a 'blind spot' rather than a perplexity effect. (5) Raise the mirror reader to 12 seeds or state its result as descriptive; at 6 seeds with an unknown reader-E clean gain the arm that separates proximity from a writer property is the weakest cell in the design. (6) Add one contamination rate below 0.5 (0.1 or 0.2, the realistic regime for a success-filtered shared store) to the confirmatory plan instead of only the optional rate-1.0 slope. (7) Publish the game-versus-seed variance decomposition from Measurement A/C before pre-registering the +/-3.3 margins.
missing_baseline: A decorrelated same-backbone judge. The plan uses Q-prox variants as writers but never as judges, so 'foreign judge' is always a different backbone, and P5's conclusion ('writer identity is a required field; you need a second model') is untested against the cheapest thing a practitioner would try first: Q itself at a different temperature, a different scaffold, an ensemble of self-consistency samples, or Q asked about the item framed as a third party's trajectory. If a re-scaffolded or ensembled Q recovers most of the harm that the own-judgment filter misses, the foreign-backbone story collapses to 'any decorrelated judge', and P3's diagonal becomes a prompting artifact rather than a backbone property. Adding this judge column costs no new episodes - it reuses the same 600 items at the same operating point. Secondary omissions a reviewer will also name: a reader-likelihood/perplexity ranking filter as a model-free detector (the terminal-line regex is a straw detector, recall 0 at L0 by construction), and a low contamination rate.

Three unverifiable ids out of nine in a Related Work whose job is to establish that nobody has done this is a weakness in itself. Judgment of the proposal's own check: it is above average for this pipeline - it names its channel, its queries, its retries and its ids, and it verified its closest named method by id, which most submissions do not. But it searched the wrong home vocabulary. It went to pseudo-label confirmation bias and missed the literature that actually owns its mechanism: the self-correction blind spot (2507.02778, and the 2026 formal account 2607.09803 that its own novelty card surfaced at the top and it does not discuss), self-preference in LLM judges (2410.21819, 2608.18091), and model-similarity-limits-oversight (2502.04313). It also missed 2606.24428, a June 2026 preprint that is the nearest recent work to its cross-judge remedy in exactly its setting. Novelty is therefore scored on what survives: the harm half (P1/P2 - proximity-graded harm with a mirror reader and a manufactured, non-adversarial contaminant) is unmeasured in what I verified; the detection half (P3/P4) and the filter (P5) are transpositions of documented effects and an existing recipe.
